problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot 1+7\cdot 0+3\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot (-2)}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 2+7\cdot 3+3\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{1\cdot 0+7\cdot (-1)+3\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 3}{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}{a}_{3}=(-\frac{1}{2})[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+(-\frac{1}{2})[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 6 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+(-1)[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 10 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x$ or any other non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ 

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}\,x}{‖x‖\,‖{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x‖} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 4+7\cdot 5+3\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-2)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{49}{\sqrt{63}\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{49}{3\sqrt{7}\cdot 7} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3})≈{28.13}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
